LD 1542 An Act to Amend the Membership of the Washington County Budget Advisory Committee

Dear committee members and respective chairs, please allow me to introduce myself as Christopher Gardner, former longtime Chairman of the Washington County Commissioners, a position I held from 2005 through December of 2024. This past election cycle I made the difficult decision to not run for re-election after 20 years of service.
As one can imagine, in my many years as County Commissioner I was deeply involved in the budget process for Washington County and can speak with some knowledge on the budget committee and its budget process. Adding to that is the fact that I am also a lifelong resident of the Washington County Unorganized Territories in Edmunds Township. It was in these two capacities that I reached out to Senator Moore in favor of the changes being proposed in LD1542, most specifically around the UT representation on the committee.
What some do not realize is that the Unorganized Territories are the single biggest county taxpaying entity in Washington County year after year. Despite this however, where other municipalities, both large and small, have the opportunity to seek a direct municipal representative on the budget committee, the Unorganized Territories do not. This is due to the fact that the municipal government entity for the UT's are by statue the County Commissioners, who do not serve directly on the committee.
In my role as County Commissioner representing Washington County's 2nd District, I represented some of the most populated of the County UT's. Although I did my best to objectively represent the UT interests in the budget process, one could argue that the duality of the role as both municipal representative of the UTs and also as a County Commissioner for the District as whole, was somewhat of a conflict of interest. Seeing that as a Commissioner I had responsibility to the operational needs of the County and as such had to temper that balance that with the tax considerations and service needs of the UT residents.
For instance, when law enforcement spending was highly debated in years past, in my role in budget discussions, if I were to advocate for higher or lower spending, was that for the "County" or was that in consideration of what the UT resident's saw as the needs the territories face? I was fortunate that my long standing and well-known position as a UT resident and Commissioner allowed me to navigate those fine lines, but it always remained a point of conflict.
Senator Moore's bill allows that to be simplified. For matters of the budget process, the UT's as a whole should have the right to be represented at the same level of any other municipal entity of Washington County as laid out in LD1542.

Coupling this with the fact that this additional member of the committee would allow the "numbers to work" in that the County Delegation representative can be returned once again to its rightful place as a voting member. This by way of bringing the total budget committee voting membership to 11 and thusly keeping it at an odd number for instances of avoiding "tie votes" on matters. This odd number issue has been seen as important in previous legislation around this budget committee.
As I close, I will say that although I no longer officially represent the people of Washington County, my record of multiple elections, with the last three being unopposed, with humility I would like to believe I have always been known to have a good sense of what the people of Washington County would be supportive of. It is with this experience, and in my capacity as a lifelong UT resident, that I would encourage the committee to offer LD1542 its fullest support.
Sincerely,
Christopher M. Gardner (Former) Washington County Commissioner District 2

Re: LD 1542, An Act to Amend the Membership of the Washington County Budget Advisory Committee
Dear Members of the State and Local Government Committee:
On behalf of the Maine County Commissioners Association, we appreciate the opportunity to provide testimony to the Committee in support of LD 1542. This legislation aims to improve representation, transparency, and input in the county budgeting process.
About MCCA. Briefly, the Maine County Commissioners Association was established in 1890 to assist Maine's county government in providing vital services to Maine citizens in a responsive, efficient, and credible manner. The Association is based in Augusta, represents all 16 of Maine's counties, and is governed by a board with representation from each participating county.
What does LD 1542 do? This legislation proposes thoughtful amendments to the composition of the Washington County Budget Advisory Committee by:
1. Appointing a resident from the unorganized territory in Washington County as a voting member for a three-year term; and
2. Modifying the role of the Washington County legislative delegation member from a nonvoting to a voting member, selected biennially for a two-year term.
Discussion. These changes aim to enhance representation and transparency in the county's budgetary process. By including a resident from the unorganized territory, the bill ensures that all areas within the county have a voice in fiscal decisions. Transitioning the legislative delegate to a voting member further strengthens the collaborative relationship between county and state governance. MCCA believes that these adjustments will lead to a more inclusive and effective budget advisory committee, better reflecting the diverse interests of Washington County's constituents.
Conclusion. We respectfully ask the Committee to support this legislation. Thank you, and please let us know if you have questions or need additional information.
Respectfully submitted,

Good morning, Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government. l\/ly name
is Marianne Moore. I proudly represent Senate District 6 which includes all of Washington County and 16 Communities in Eastern Hancock County as well.

I'm here to introduce LD1542 -- An Act to Amend the Membership of the Washington
County Budget Advisory Committee.

To provide a little background, Washington County (WC) has three (3) Commissioner
Districts. By statute, the WC Budget Advisory Committee (BAC) consists of at least
three (3) municipal officers from each district "unless the municipal officers of a
`
district decide that another person from that district would be more qualified" i.e. a
Finance Director. Each serves a 3-year term. Additionally, the statute includes one
WC legislative delegate, selected annually by the WC Delegation. Prior to 2019, the legislative delegate was a voting member of the WC BAC. This resulted in the total
number of available votes for a budget of ten (10), obviously an even number. I
believe Representative Will Tuell served this role during his initial tenure in the
House.

Apparently, this even number didn't pose a problem until a version of the County Budget became somewhat debatable and resulted in a 5 to 5 vote, failing passage
thus the introduction of legislation changing the legislative delegate to a non-voting
member to bring the voting numbers to an odd ratio.

Since I was elected in 2019, l have served on the WC BAC not necessarily "elected"

but more "in the absence of any other 'v0lunteer"' . While l have attempted to
attend most of the meetings and am able to ask questions, make comments, etc., it is very frustrating not to be able to vote on the budget especially when we saw an

increase of 21.96% this year. While I understand why the statute was changed, l have submitted this bill to make changes to the statute regarding the membership of the
WC Budget Advisory Committee.

The first portion of the bill firms up the selection of the WC legislative delegate,
patterning the wording similar to what was approved for Hancock County's Budget Advisory Committee in LD893 in 2023. It requires the Washington County legislative delegation to select by majority vote, by October 15, 2025, and by October 15th of
every odd-numbered year thereafter, one member of the delegation who resides in
Washington County to serve on the budget advisory committee for a 2-year term as a
VOTING member.
The second portion of the bill importantly adds an additional member to the WC BAC,
representing the Unorganized Territories (UT) of WC, who would serve a 3-year term similar to the municipal members of the Budget Committee.
Besides bringing the membership numbers to eleven (11), more importantly, this gives a voice to the 35 UTs in the County. Currently they are represented by a "Supervisor" in the County Government, reporting to the Commissioners. Their portion of the overall County Budget is the largest contributor of close to 10% based on their total property valuations. The next closest municipality is Baileyville, with the Woodland Mill and St. Croix Tissue Plant, at 7.5%. See the attached Proposed Tax by Town for the year 2025.
Statistically, the UTs are the single biggest taxpayers in the county, and, yet, they have no direct representation on the Budget Committee other than the
commissioners who act based on the recommendation of the Budget Committee. Why shouldn't the largest contributing group have a say in the final budget spending
numbers for the County?
I ask for your support of this bill and would be happy to answer any questions you might have!
Thank you!
